proposed.explanation: Edita's consolidated net profit grew from 1,606,727,698 EGP in 2024 to 2,695,301,670 EGP in 2025, an increase of 1,088,573,972 EGP or approximately 67.8%. This exceeds your 50% threshold, so your condition for buying more is met. However, I cannot recommend a buy because of the portfolio diversification rule. Your current EFID position (1,000 shares × 20.40 EGP = 20,400 EGP) already represents 67.1% of your total portfolio value (20,400 + 10,000 cash = 30,400 EGP), which is well above the 50% single-company cap. Buying even one additional share would push the concentration further over the limit, and the rule allows no exceptions. The responsible course is to hold your existing 1,000 shares and keep the 10,000 EGP cash as a buffer. If you wish to add to EFID in the future, you would first need to either sell some EFID to bring the position below 50% of total portfolio value, or allocate new funds to other holdings so that EFID's share of the portfolio falls below the cap. Note: the 2025 net-profit figure on page 6 is partially obscured by a stamp in one scan (evidence p6-30, marked AMBIGUOUS), but the same figure is clearly legible and verified in a separate extraction (p6-36), so the calculation above is reliable. Risks: a single-year profit jump does not guarantee continued growth; the 3-year horizon means you will be exposed to at least one more full earnings cycle, and medium loss tolerance means a sharp correction in EFID's share price could erode the 20,400 EGP you already hold. This is guidance, not a guarantee of returns.
